title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We measure how inserting a deterministic network verifier into a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) loop affects verifier-detected safety violations for LLM-produced device-configuration proposals. In a preregistered paired design (N = 500 intent→configuration tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters) we compared: (1) baseline — a single LLM proposal produced once per task, and (2) guarded — the identical shared LLM proposal validated by a deterministic netops verifier and subjected to up to one automated repair iteration if the verifier flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). The preregistered exact McNemar two-sided test was implemented as an exact binomial on discordant pairs (n = n10 + n01); with n = 1 and n10 = 1 the archived two-sided p = 1.00 under that convention. Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; measured marginal verifier+repair effect on the pass-rate metric is therefore small, though the verifier corrected at least one concrete baseline failure. All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are being applied to NetOps tasks including operator-intent translation to device configuration, multi-step change planning, and automated repair. System reports and reviews emphasize that operational safety is determined largely by surrounding engineering (deterministic validators, sandboxed replay, canarying, and rollback mechanisms) rather than by model outputs alone [Beckett et al., 2017; Wei et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. A common operational pattern is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): an LLM proposes a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks a set of formalized properties, and automated or human-guided repairs are applied when violations are found. Practically useful guidance for deployers requires controlled measurements of the verifier’s marginal contribution (holding the LLM proposal fixed). We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment that isolates the verifier+repair impact under canonical deterministic semantics. The research question: given identical initial proposals (shared-initial_candidate semantics), how much does integrating a deterministic verifier and at most one automated repair iteration reduce verifier-detected safety violations compared to the same LLM alone?
sections.related_work: Formal, deterministic verification methods for network configurations and updates (header-space analysis and route-model verifiers) provide machine-checkable properties such as reachability, isolation, and update atomicity; they underpin operational verifier-in-the-loop designs [Beckett et al., 2017]. Recent NetOps/AIOps and intent-translation work has integrated LLMs while advocating guardrails to improve operational reliability (e.g., INTA, Confucius, and other agentic NetOps frameworks) [INTA, 2025; Wang et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. Generate–verify–repair or generate–critic architectures are widely proposed across structured-generation domains to reduce incorrect outputs [PoeTone; INTA]. Separate literature documents LLM failure modes (hallucination, theatrical compliance, tool-integration errors) and motivates verification or human oversight to mitigate outages [Owen, 2026; DeepSeek-AI, 2025]. What is absent in the supplied evidence is a controlled, preregistered ablation that quantifies the marginal verifier effect while keeping the LLM’s initial output identical for both arms; this study provides such an artifact-backed measurement.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. We preregistered study_id cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026, freezing the research question, inclusion/exclusion rules, deterministic generator seeds, estimands, analysis executor, multiplicity plan, retry policy, and stopping rule prior to observing outcomes. Primary confirmatory hypothesis: an LLM paired with a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair iteration will produce a lower verifier-detected safety-violation rate than the same LLM producing a single proposal without verifier feedback (paired within-task). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where success == verifier reports zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations. The preregistration and all supporting artifacts are archived (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest).

Task corpus and strata. A deterministic synthetic corpus of 500 intent→configuration tasks was generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 with preregistered seeds and stratified per the preregistration. The realized per-cluster sample sizes matched the preregistration allocation: VLAN-change = 167, ACL-change = 167, static-route-change = 166. The generator constrained allowed features to {admin, mtu, vlan} to match the verifier’s modeled scope; the full task manifest (inputs, seeds, expected_final_state, required_sequence) is archived under execution/task_manifest.jsonl. The preregistration specified deterministic replacement rules for excluded or duplicate tasks; no confirmatory exclusions or deviations occurred (deviations_from_preregistration = []).

Generation semantics, model, and verifier. To isolate the verifier’s marginal effect we used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (independent_condition_generation = false): a single shared LLM proposal was produced per task; that identical candidate served as the baseline output and was also validated by the guarded arm. The guarded path invoked the single automated repair call only if the deterministic verifier reported a preregistered high/medium-severity violation on the shared candidate. Requested LLM = gpt-5-mini called through the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter; configuration (max_output_tokens = 2000, single attempt) is archived in execution/model_configuration.json. The deterministic verifier used was deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator specification and violation-code→severity mapping archived). Repair budget: at most one automated repair iteration per preregistered contract.

Primary statistical test and implementation. The preregistered confirmatory test is the paired exact McNemar two-sided test on binary pass/fail outcomes. The archived analysis executor implements the two-sided exact test by enumerating discordant pairs n = n10 + n01 and performing an exact binomial two-sided test on the observed count n10 under X ∼ Binomial(n, 0.5). Concretely: p_two_sided = 2 × min{P(X ≤ n10), P(X ≥ n10)} (truncated at 1.0). The analysis implementation and parameters are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (bootstrap and hypothesis-testing code paths). For CI estimation we used a paired-bootstrap percentile CI with B = 10,000 resamples and bootstrap_seed = 1729; resampling unit = paired task.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes. The run completed with complete_pair_count = 500 and model_calls_used = 501 (shared_initial_generation = 500; repair-stage calls = 1). Aggregated per-condition counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded_success_rate = 1.000). The paired contingency (guarded × baseline) is: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002.

Exact test and CI. Using the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention yields two-sided p = 1.00 for the observed discordant counts (n = 1, n10 = 1). The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute difference is [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). The analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json and CSVs) and analysis_log.jsonl record these computations and parameters.

Discordant episode provenance and repair summary. Exactly one discordant pair exists (guarded pass, baseline fail). The discordant episode identifier and the full per-task traces (validator_trace, repair_provider_trace, provider-call traces, normalized configurations) are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl and execution/provider_calls/*. To deterministically locate the episode: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for entries where baseline scoring indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) while guarded scoring indicates pass == 1. The run-level manifests (deterministic_reconciliation.json and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) confirm exactly one such episode and model_calls_used = 501 with a single repair-stage call. For the discordant episode the archived validator_trace shows an initial preregistered medium/high-severity violation (violation codes and severity mapping are in the validator-spec artifacts) and the guarded repair call produced a modified candidate that the verifier subsequently evaluated as valid (no high/medium-severity violations). The verbatim provider-call traces and validator diagnostics for that episode are available in the evidence bundle for auditors; to avoid reproducing provider traces in the paper body we summarize the artifact-backed outcome as: verifier initially flagged a preregistered violation in the modeled property set and the automated repair adjusted the shared candidate such that the verifier re-evaluated it as valid.

Power and ceiling effects. The preregistration assumed a baseline failure prevalence near 0.30 to compute required N (≈384 for 80% power to detect a 10 percentage-point improvement). Observed baseline failure prevalence (1/500) was far lower, producing a ceiling effect that limited sensitivity to detect small absolute improvements. Consequently the small number of discordant pairs rendered the exact-test p-value non-informative for rejecting the null despite a non-zero point estimate; the paired-bootstrap CI provides complementary uncertainty quantification.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and operational implications. Under the constrained experimental regime — single requested LLM (gpt-5-mini), shared_initial_candidate semantics (identical proposals), a deterministic verifier modeling a limited feature set (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}), and at most one automated repair iteration — the LLM produced near-ceiling correct proposals and the marginal measured pass-rate benefit of adding the verifier was small (0.002). This conditional measurement shows that when baseline proposal quality is very high for the verifier-scoped properties, a modest verifier+repair budget may yield negligible marginal pass-rate gains on a composite pass/fail metric, although the verifier can still correct rare but concrete baseline failures (one observed here).

Design-choice consequences. The shared_initial_candidate semantics were chosen intentionally to isolate the verifier+repair effect conditional on identical proposals (useful when deployment semantics require a single human-reviewed proposal to be repaired rather than regenerated). This design does not evaluate alternative operational choices such as verifier-guided regeneration, multiple repair iterations, or non-binary cost-weighted objectives; those alternatives may yield larger effect sizes and require separate preregistrations.

Threats to validity. Internal validity benefits from preregistration, deterministic seeds, and automated replacement rules; no manual adjudication occurred and no confirmatory exclusions were taken. Construct validity is limited to the verifier’s covered property set — pass==no preregistered high/medium-severity violations is defined relative to that coverage and severity mapping archived in the validator-spec artifacts. External validity is limited by single-model testing, the synthetic task corpus, and constrained feature scope; results do not imply multi-model or cross-vendor generality.

Recommendations. (1) Measure baseline error prevalence on representative operational workloads before committing engineer-hours to repair budgets; when baseline error is extremely low for verifier-modeled properties, marginal pass-rate gains per unit cost may be small. (2) Align verifier coverage to operator-critical constraints and expand the modeled property set where needed. (3) Select generation semantics to match operational priorities: shared-initial semantics minimize model calls and preserve original proposals for human review, whereas verifier-guided regeneration can raise final-pass probability at higher model-call cost.

Reproducibility. All run artifacts are archived: preregistration, deterministic task generator and seeds, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/provider_calls/*, execution/model_configuration.json, validator-spec artifacts, analysis CSVs, deterministic_reconciliation.json, and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (which documents hypothesis-test code paths and bootstrap parameters). The preregistered initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).
sections.conclusion: We performed a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment (N = 500) that isolated the verifier+single-repair effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The LLM-produced proposals were near-ceiling for the verifier-modeled properties (baseline 499/500; guarded 500/500), yielding an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]; archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the run’s exact-binomial convention). This conditional measurement illustrates a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality is very high and verifier coverage is limited, the measurable marginal pass-rate benefit of a modest verifier+repair budget can be negligible on a composite pass/fail metric, though the verifier can still correct rare concrete failures. Practitioners should measure baseline error prevalence, align verifier coverage with operator-critical properties, and choose generation/repair semantics that match deployment priorities. All artifacts and traces supporting these claims are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection.

limitations: Synthetic, deterministic task corpus limited to features modeled by the deterministic validator; task payloads constrained to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}. Results do not generalize to unconstrained production intents, cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or protocol semantics outside the verifier scope.
Single requested model family (gpt-5-mini requested) and a single validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — no claim of multi-model or cross-validator generality is made.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets or iterative regeneration strategies could change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) created a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention and the small discordant count.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl in the evidence bundle. To inspect it deterministically: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair entries where the baseline scoring outcome indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) while the guarded scoring outcome indicates pass == 1; because only one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this lookup returns the single episode and its provider-call traces. The validator violation-code→severity mapping is archived in the execution manifest and validator-spec artifacts in the bundle.
